title: All Star Western Theatre
paragraphs: A Western variety program combining short frontier dramas, comedy, music by Foy Willing and the Riders of the Purple Sage, and appearances by Western film personalities.

Half-hour Western variety combining short dramas/comedy, Western music by Foy Willing and the Riders of the Purple Sage, and rotating film/radio guest stars. Surviving material also includes syndicated transcriptions.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS Pacific / KNX era (August 11, 1946 to February 14, 1948) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]] and Don Lee / Mutual / KHJ era (February 21, 1948 to August 14, 1948) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Foy Willing and The Riders Of The Purple Sage (performer), Cottonseed Clark (announcer and performer), Terry O'Sullivan (announcer), Harry Lang (performer), Monty Montana (performer and guest), Joe Forte (performer), and Don Diamond (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]], [[org|org.7027e8a3676e0d84|KNX]], [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]], [[org|org.87e6f64937f0bfb8|KHJ]], and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].
The stories often return to Western music and cowboy songs, frontier West, ranching and cowboy life, rodeo and horsemanship, outlaws and frontier crime, and Western film-star culture.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar Western film/radio star crossover, Network airchecks and syndicated transcription afterlife, and Regional sponsor-driven Western variety.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], and [[show|wild-bill-hickok|Wild Bill Hickok]].
